schemes.official_name: College of Engineering Industry Capstone Program
schemes.english_name: College of Engineering Industry Capstone Program
schemes.description: Sponsor organisations propose projects, reviewed by College of Engineering faculty; students are matched to an approved project and faculty mentor and run a full-scale design process January-June, with a weekly technical mentor from the sponsor; final showcase in June. Sponsors pay project costs plus an $18,000 program fee.

schemes.unresolved: Whether the program is compulsory (departmental capstones); credit; partner_type typed Business as sponsors are companies, but sector mix beyond the AeroVironment example was not itemised; further departmental capstones (ME, EE, BioE) likely overlap.

profile_md: Several distributed, mostly faculty/programme-level routes were verified at UW (page text via WebFetch, 2026-10-13). The strongest: the College of Engineering Industry Capstone (sponsor-proposed, sponsor-funded team projects January-June with weekly sponsor technical mentor; 54 sponsors/95 projects/550+ students in 2023/24); the Evans School Student Consulting Lab (second-year MPA teams of 3-5 consulting for public, private and nonprofit clients over five months); and Foster CBDC undergraduate consulting courses MGMT 440/445 (4-5 student teams for real small-business clients, 4 credits, 10 weeks). Biostatistics MS capstone treats sponsors as clients (undated page). Livable City Year links a city/county partner with multi-disciplinary courses annually (2026-27: Seattle and Jefferson County) but team structure is not shown. The iSchool Informatics Capstone allows individual or group work with optional sponsors, so evidence is incomplete. Participation is compulsory only within some programmes (probably Evans MPA); there is no university-wide employer-project requirement. CELE community engagement is individual internship/service-learning and is excluded. Clients at Foster CBDC are external businesses though the centre is a school unit. Uncertain: current status of several undated pages, compulsory status of capstones.
gaps: Further departmental instances likely (Mechanical/Electrical/Bioengineering capstones, HCDE, Foster MBA Global Consulting Projects and MSCM team projects, Built Environments studios, law and health clinics, Bothell/Tacoma campuses) - not researched in reduced-depth mode. Health and law clinics were not queried (other area covered via built environments only). Engineering program credit/compulsory status and team size not stated. Some figures come from search extracts (labelled).
